business_scope.primary_industry_name: Tier-3/4 Server Rack Space Leasing and Bare-Metal Server Hosting

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Civil Law statutory core (Spanish tradition) with Common Law-style corporate statutes (Ley 32 de 1927 modeled on Delaware corporate law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States - Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA; in force 31 October 2012)
Canada - Panama Free Trade Agreement (in force 1 April 2013)
Panama - United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (in force 1 January 2019)
Panama - Republic of China (Taiwan) Free Trade Agreement (in force 1 January 2004)

Panama is additionally party to 20+ bilateral investment treaties (inter alia with the Netherlands, Switzerland, Spain, Republic of Korea, Singapore and the People's Republic of China) and is a full WTO member

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (Panama's central AML/CFT statute), as amended by Ley No. 70 de 30 de enero de 2019 (beneficial-ownership reporting, resident-agent duties and predicate-offense expansion); UBO filings implemented through the e-UBO module and resolutions of the Registro Público de Panamá; supervision by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) under the Consejo Nacional de Lucha contra el Lavado de Activos; supplemental customer due diligence rules in Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá Acuerdo No. 3-2018; framework aligned with FATF Recommendations 10, 24 and 25.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry / competent authority of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Convention) or, for non-Hague jurisdictions, Panamanian Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Register of Directors and Officers of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company secretary or registered agent of the corporate shareholder in its home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille / Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution of the corporate shareholder authorizing (i) incorporation of the Sociedad Anónima, (ii) appointment of the resident agent, and (iii) opening of banking arrangements
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Corporate seal, notarization plus Hague Apostille / Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (Poder Especial) appointing the Panamanian resident agent and legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate shareholder acting through its legal representatives
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized and apostilled / consular legalized; accepted for local registration use

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of passports of directors and ultimate beneficial owners, together with the sworn UBO declaration (Declaración de Beneficiario Final)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority of each individual; sworn declaration executed before a Panamanian notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization; passports must be translated into Spanish by a Panamanian sworn translator

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, signatories, resident agents and material counterparties against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, the UN Security Council consolidated list (ISIL and Al-Qaida 1267/1989 regime and successor regimes), the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Panama's national designation list (Lista de Personas Designadas maintained by the UAF). Domestic and foreign Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) require Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD), independent source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, and senior management approval before onboarding. Ongoing transaction monitoring and suspicious-transaction reporting are mandatory under Ley 23 de 2015.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Sede Electrónica (https://www.registro-publico.gob.pa); corporate name queries and reservations processed through the Mercantile Section ('Calificaciones' / 'Avisos de Operación')
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: S.A. names may be adopted in Spanish or any foreign language; where the corporate name uses non-Latin script, a Spanish transliteration must be provided at filing. The name must end with the appropriate corporate identifier (e.g., 'S.A.', 'Corp.', 'Inc.', 'Holdings') and must not be identical or deceptively similar to any existing registered entity, trademark or registered trade name in Panama.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: BANCO / FINANCIERA (prior authorization of the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá required)
SEGUROS / REASEGUROS (prior authorization of the Superintendencia de Seguros y Reaseguros required)
MINISTERIO / GOBIERNO / NACIONAL / OFICIAL (implying state affiliation)
CORREOS / TELÉGRAFOS (implying any official monopoly service)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the requested S.A. name is rejected for duplication, deceptive similarity or use of a prohibited token, the applicant must file a written reconsideration request (recurso de reconsideración) within ten (10) business days before the Dirección General del Registro Público under Ley 38 de 2000, attaching: (a) the registry's refusal notice, (b) a revised name variation, and (c) trademark or 'aviso de operación' evidence where the name has been used in commerce. If the reconsideration is denied, a hierarchical appeal (recurso de apelación) may be lodged within five (5) business days; judicial recourse lies before the contentious-administrative chamber of the Corte Suprema de Justicia within two (2) months. Concurrent re-filing of an alternative name is a fast-track remedy available without prejudice to the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible at the registry level because the licensed resident agent's Panama address satisfies the registered-office requirement under Ley 32 de 1927. However, for a data-center colocation leasing vehicle, Panamanian banks and the Dirección General de Ingresos will expect demonstrable operational substance, including signed colocation/rack-leasing agreements, hosting delivery protocols, certified invoices to anchor tenants and board minutes evidencing decision-making; a purely virtual shell would likely fail Enhanced Due Diligence and may attract economic-substance scrutiny.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for this Low_Risk_Standard industry (ISIC 6209 - data center colocation): estimated less than 10% probability of an unannounced physical UAF/Registro inspection within the first 24 months absent a suspicious-transaction trigger. The probability may increase to approximately 15-20% if the company opens multiple Panamanian banking relationships or processes high-volume Swift wires inconsistent with rack-leasing turnover. UAF conducts risk-based on-site supervision under Ley 23 de 2015.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Panama General Corporation Law (Ley 32 de 26 de febrero de 1927, as amended), especially Articles 1 through 62, supplemented by the Código de Comercio and the Regulations of the Registro Público de Panamá on qualification of corporate instruments
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Dirección General de Registros, Sección de Personas (Companies and Legal Entities Registry)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública containing the Pacto Social y Estatutos (Articles of Incorporation), notarially protocolized and inscribed in the Registro Público de Panamá
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Sociedad Anónima; the charter sets an authorized capital (customarily US$10,000), of which at least one share must be subscribed and issued at formation; subscription payments are governed solely by the charter, with no escrow or deposit account mandate at incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Board of Directors of [Panama S.A.], acting under Ley 32 de 1927 and the Articles of Incorporation, hereby: (1) Approve the subscription and issuance of the initial authorized shares, recording payment in the Share Subscription Book; (2) Adopt the registered office in Panama and ratify the appointment of the Registered Agent (Agente Residente) for service of process; (3) Appoint the President, Treasurer, and Secretary as statutory officers, with joint signing powers for contracts, banking, and registry filings; (4) Ratify all preparatory acts and authorize the Secretary to present this resolution for registration in the corporate Minutes Book. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - electronic filing office and Directorate General of Registries
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit via the Registro Público electronic portal a name-search application listing at least three proposed denominations with the S.A. suffix; the registry verifies identical or similar existing names nationally and abroad. Upon availability, the chosen name is reserved for a thirty-day preferential term and a search certificate is issued.
required_dossiers: Completed name-search application
Identity document of the incorporating promoter
Three alternative proposed corporate names with S.A. suffix
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is refused for similarity or prior reservation, file immediately a new search request with alternative names; administrative review of a wrongful refusal may be addressed to the Director General of the Registro within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Protocolization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama (civil circuit of the incorporators' domicile)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Pacto Social y Estatutos incorporating all statutory clauses: corporate name, registered office, duration, corporate purpose covering data-center colocation and server-hosting services, authorized capital, classes of shares, incorporators' rights, resident agent, and board powers; the incorporators appear before the notary, subscribe the initial shares, and the instrument is protocolized as a public deed or private instrument.
required_dossiers: Valid passports or national identity cards of the incorporators
Name-search certificate
Final draft of the charter and bylaws
Signed acceptance letter of the Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notarial observations on form or capacity are cured by signing a corrective addendum before the same notary; if the reservation expires, renew the name certificate and re-execute the instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration and Qualification at the Registro Público de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Section of Legal Persons (Sociedades Anónimas)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the protocolized incorporation instrument, applicable fiscal stamps, and the official filing form at the registry's presentation window or through the electronic desk; the registry qualifies the instrument and, upon approval, assigns the permanent inscription folio number (F.D. number) of the Sociedad Anónima.
required_dossiers: Protocolized Escritura Pública or private instrument
Registration application form of the Registro Público
Payment receipt of the state filing fee
Fiscal stamps and municipal timbres where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a defect or objection notice is issued, cure the deficiencies by filing the requested corrective clauses and exhibits through the same presentation window; a qualified denial may be appealed to the Director General del Registro Público within the statutory appeal term.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of the Folio Certificate and Opening of Statutory Corporate Books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - certificates and corporate books offices; the S.A. acting through its Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Order the certified certificate of the inscription (testimonio/certificado de registro) evidencing legal existence; draft, notarize, and present the statutory corporate books - Share Subscription and Transfer Register, Shareholders' Minutes Book, Directors' Minutes Book, and Accounting Ledgers - for foliation and stamping by the Registro Público; then record the first board resolution approving share subscription, registered office, and officers.
required_dossiers: Written request for the certificate of inscription
Statutory corporate books for foliation
First board resolution (minutes)
Official receipts of registry book fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry returns the books for correction, re-notarize the defective folios and re-present for stamping; incorrect certificates are rectified through the registry certificate-correction desk at no additional substantive burden.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Taxpayer Enrollment with the Dirección General de Ingresos (RUC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the initial RUC registration in the DGI digital platform for the newly incorporated S.A., indicating the corporate legal form, the anticipated economic activity (rental of data-center rack space and colocation hosting), and the appointed legal representative; obtain the RUC certificate and activate the taxpayer digital mailbox (B-Matic).
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation (testimonio folio)
RUC registration application form
Simple or extended power of attorney of the legal representative
Valid identity document of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI issues an inconsistency or deficiency notice, correct the registry file electronically within ten working days; a rejected application can be resubmitted, or an administrative review can be requested before the Director General de Ingresos.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Aviso de Operación and Governance Organization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía del Distrito / Municipality of the data-center site (patents and avisos office); corporate bodies of the S.A.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the commercial establishment with the competent municipality and obtain the Aviso de Operación (municipal operating license) subject to annual renewal; in parallel, convene the organizational meeting of the shareholders and board to approve the share issuance, ratify the statutory officers, and close the governance record, all documented in the stamped Minutes Book.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate and DGI taxpayer data print
Certificate of incorporation
Lease agreement or property title of the data-center premises
Fire-safety inspection certificate
Municipal application form and aviso fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality objects on zoning or land-use grounds, obtain a land-use certification from the Dirección de Urbanismo or relocate the registered establishment; resubmit the corrected application within the municipal operating license window.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; taxpayer portal: DGI e-Tax / T@ Pagas (https://dgi.mef.gob.pa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must appoint a Panamanian resident agent or legal representative, execute a public deed or private document recognized by Panamanian counsel, and file registration with the DGI to obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) and ITBMS VAT registration before commencing commercial activity. Registration is performed through the T@ Pagas online portal using a digital signature.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. Panama's Tax Code does not provide a domestic hybrid mismatch election. Affiliated Panamanian corporations may elect consolidated income tax filing under Law 52 of 2013, subject to DGI authorization and fulfillment of ownership and common-control requirements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) — VAT/GST
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No statutory turnover threshold; any person or entity making taxable transfers of goods or providing taxable services in Panama, including non-residents with Panamanian-source nexus, must register for RUC and ITBMS before the first taxable operation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing under the DGI's 'Facturación Electrónica' regime. Taxpayers must use DGI-approved electronic invoicing software or connect via the DGI validation platform's API web services to transmit invoices in near real time for pre-issuance authorization. Each authorized invoice must display a unique authorization number or CUFE plus a QR code/digital stamp; non-compliant invoices are not valid for tax credit or deduction purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% ITBMS) is available for exports of movable goods physically shipped outside Panama and for services rendered and effectively used entirely outside Panama. To qualify, the taxpayer must substantiate that the benefit of the service is not derived from Panamanian territory. Data center colocation services performed at a Panamanian facility do not automatically qualify; the DGI may allow zero-rating only where the service is structured as a genuine offshore service with foreign consumption, supported by executed contracts and certificates of service delivery abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación de Mercancías)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Remesa de Divisas) or bank transfer evidence
Foreign service contract and/or Certificate of Services Rendered Abroad (for offshore services)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI may audit zero-rated transactions for up to five years; failure to substantiate export or offshore service status results in full VAT clawback at 7%, plus monthly late-payment interest (approximately 3% per month) and penalties ranging from 25% to 200% of the omitted tax. Willful fraudulent claims constitute tax evasion under the Panamanian Penal Code and may lead to monetary fines and imprisonment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no central bank. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP), created under Decree Law No. 2 of 2008, is the banking and FX market regulator and supervises authorisation, capital, and AML/CFT compliance of all licensed banks. Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent and public-sector clearing agent but holds no monetary policy or exchange control authority. The Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF), established under Law 23 of 2015, is the national financial intelligence unit for cross-border funds surveillance. The Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) administers taxation but exercises no FX control function.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility by statute and by design. The Panamanian Balboa (PAB) is a currency unit fixed 1:1 to the US Dollar, and USD notes and coins are legal tender throughout the Republic. There is no legal distinction between capital-account and current-account transactions, no exchange licence regime, and no prior authorisation for dividend distributions, loan repayments, or capital disinvestment. The only remittance impediment is fiscal, not monetary: dividends distributed from Panama-source income of a territorial-tax Sociedad Anónima are subject to 10% withholding under Law 52 of 2012, whereas distributions funded from foreign-source income are not subject to remittance-linked taxation. A colocation entity whose servers and rack-leasing activity are physically situated in Panama will be treated as generating Panama-source income; profit repatriation to a foreign parent is freely executable via SWIFT within 3-5 business days once the applicable 10% dividend tax is declared and settled under the company's RUC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Panama imposes no statutory surrender, mandatory conversion, or repatriation deadline on export receipts or service income. Monthly colocation and bare-metal hosting revenues received from offshore anchor tenants in USD remain immediately available for operating expenditures, debt service, capex, or shareholder distributions without reporting to the SBP, the UAF, or the MEF. For corporate tax purposes the revenue is taxable in Panama because the servers, network equipment, and colocation halls are physically located within Panamanian territory; however, no FX conversion or delivery obligation attaches to those proceeds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (USD corporate demand deposit with corporate ACH and SWIFT wire modules)
Operational Account (state fiscal-agent bank; advantageous for public-sector data centre contracts)
Operational Account with direct U.S. correspondent clearing and optional Capital Escrow Account for a compliance-mandated initial capitalisation lockbox (3-to-6-month enhanced due diligence period)
Operational Account (corporate checking with Panama ACH and SWIFT connectivity)
Operational Account plus optional Capital Escrow Account for client security deposits handled under escrow-as-a-service instructions
Operational Account (Grupo Aval affiliate; strong correspondent coverage for Colombia and Central American tenant corridors)
Operational Account (mid-market corporate desk accommodating foreign-director S.A.s)
Operational Account (boutique private bank; appetite limited to high-balance treasury relationships, not recurring hosting receivables)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium-Low as a primary treasury rail; acceptable only as a secondary collection layer for e-commerce ingress. Legal constraints: foreign electronic-money institutions and digital neobanks hold no Panamanian banking licence, are not supervised by the SBP, and possess no passporting rights into Panama; a Panama S.A. may lawfully open such accounts as ordinary offshore payment accounts, but Tier-1 Panamanian banks apply a reputational-risk overlay and may treat heavy treasury dependence on unlicensed EMIs as an adverse AML-CFT signal during the first 18 months after account opening. Recommended structure: connect a single EMI (Wise or Mercury-type) to card-acquiring rails for small colocation clients, execute daily sweeps of balances into the primary Panamanian operating account, and never retain more than three months of operating expenses on the EMI platform.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is legally permissible: SBP Regulation No. 005-2021 does not require an in-person appearance when the applicant submits apostilled articles of incorporation, a certified power of attorney, video-validated passports, and a notarised Resident Agent certification. In practice, onboarding committees at all Tier-1 banks materially accelerate approval if at least one director or the designated corporate officer attends a single in-person compliance interview at a Panamá City branch. Recommended mandate for this entity: one physical KYC interview by the CFO or shareholder representative before account activation, accompanied by an economic-substance file evidencing a physical footprint at the data centre premises: facility lease registered under the company's RUC, ENSA/Edemet utility invoices, fibre-optic contracts, and Caja de Seguro Social payroll declarations for at least two to five local technicians.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) from jurisdictions without prior Panamanian banking history and no visible local involvement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled passport copies; 12-month personal bank statements evidencing lawful accumulation of contribution capital; UBO declaration filed in the Registro Público beneficial-owners registry under Law 23 of 2015; curriculum vitae; signed net-worth and source-of-wealth summary; business references from two regulated foreign banks; note that Panama was removed from the FATF grey list in June 2023.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shell-company perception — a newly incorporated S.A. with a generic 'any lawful activity' purpose clause and minimal Panamanian economic footprint.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Facility lease for the Tier-3/4 data centre registered under the company's RUC; recent ENSA/Edemet electricity invoices reflecting server-hall loads; signed bandwidth and interconnect agreements with carriers (C&W/Liberty, Lumen, Telxius); board operating-resolution limiting the company's purpose to ISIC 6209 colocation and hosting; installed-rack inventory and data-hall access audit trail.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large round-number capital injection into a new account before recurring revenue history is demonstrable.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution approving the capital contribution on a scheduled call schedule; executed anchor-tenant master colocation agreement; 12-month cash-flow forecast; IFRS-ready accounting engagement letter; capital quantum explanation against fit-out, UPS, cooling, and networking capex.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commingling of client security deposits or prepaid hosting fees with the company's operating funds, raising trustee-account concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Service agreements invoicing strictly in arrears; IFRS 15 accounting policy separating trade receivables from customer deposits; a dedicated sub-ledger for any rent-in-advance modules with monthly reconciliation; executed escrow instructions to the bank if deposit balances exceed USD 5,000 per client.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment flows from or to virtual-asset service providers, unlicensed money transmitters, or FATF/CFATF-flagged jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal payment-flow matrix evidencing that all invoices are settled from regulated corporate bank accounts; written treasury policy prohibiting crypto-currency settlement for colocation fees; acceptance of client USD remittances only via SWIFT from top-tier correspondents; pre-prepared response file for any UAF transaction report triggered by an accidental unrelated credit.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Protocol: the shareholder executes a capital-contribution board resolution; funds are remitted via SWIFT MT103 from the parent's regulated bank account to the Panamanian operating account. Wire template: Field 52A (ordering institution); Field 56A (intermediary, e.g., Citibank N.A. New York or JPMorgan Chase New York for the receiving Panamanian bank); Field 59 (beneficiary: exact S.A. legal name and the bank account number — Panama does not use IBAN); Field 70 (reference: 'BOARD RESOLUTION 2025-XXXX / CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION'). Panama imposes no statutory purpose codes, no central-bank notification, and no prior approval; compliance verification is bank-driven and comprises the shareholder register update, UBO declaration, and source-of-funds evidence. For injections above USD 250,000 the bank may temporarily impose a 3-to-6-month compliance escrow overlay before free availability; treasury must pre-clear the transfer with the onboarding officer at least three business days before value date.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails are USD-dominant. (1) Domestic disbursements — data-centre facility rent, ENSA/Edemet utilities, payroll and CSS contributions, and local maintenance vendors — settle via the private ACH operated by the Panamanian Banking Association Clearing House and the Banco Nacional de Panamá government-clearing channels; execution is T+1 and fee-based for cross-bank transfers. (2) International trade payments — bandwidth backbone contracts, subsea cable carrier fees, and server imports from Dell and HPE — execute via SWIFT MT103 over Fedwire/CHIPS correspondent networks with T+0 to T+1 value; EUR-denominated European carrier invoices are paid through a multicurrency USD/EUR account at Citibank Panama. (3) Commercial letters of credit under UCP 600 are permitted and recommended only for equipment imports exceeding USD 100,000 when the supplier requires a sight LC confirmed by a foreign bank; the colocation services contract itself should never be structured as a documentary credit. Monthly invoicing uses ACH for domestic tenants and SWIFT MT103 for offshore tenants; inbound client USD is credited same-day, and remittances originating from Latin American banks routed through New York correspondents may incur one additional value date.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX spot (USD/EUR, USD/GBP, USD/CHF) executed OTC with any SBP-licensed bank; no prior Central Bank approval is required because Panama has no exchange controls; settlement is T+2 via U.S. correspondent networks (Fedwire/CHIPS) and euro-area correspondent accounts.

Deliverable FX forwards (DF) of 1-to-12-month tenor for EUR, GBP, and CHF against USD under ISDA or a local master agreement; banks require documented underlying exposure such as EUR-nominated equipment leases or European bandwidth invoices.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing Latin American currencies (COP, MXN, CLP, ARS) cash-settled in USD, offered by the international desks of Citibank Panama, BAC, and Banistmo for tenants paying in local currencies; NDFs avoid any onshore exchange-control filing by the Panamanian entity.

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) USD/EUR for synthetic conversion of a USD-denominated fit-out or infrastructure debt facility into EUR liabilities, available from Citibank Panama subject to ISDA plus credit-support annex and an approved board treasury policy.

Multicurrency deposit accounts and cash-pooling (USD/EUR/GBP/CHF) at Banco General or Citibank Panama enabling natural netting of receivable and payable currencies without derivative exposure; this passive hedge is the recommended first-line treasury strategy for a colocation business.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporation Franchise Tax (Impuesto Anual de Sociedades)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 January; if the date falls on a non-business day, payment is due on the next business day
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic 10% late-payment surcharge for the first month plus monthly interest at the legal rate for each subsequent month; non-payment blocks issuance of tax good-standing certificates; persistent arrears trigger DGI compulsory collection, asset attachment, and judicial dissolution of the S.A.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due 15 March following the close of the 31 December fiscal year; for an approved non-calendar fiscal year, within three months after the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a fine of up to USD 500 plus 10% surcharge of the tax owed and monthly interest at the statutory rate; continued failure enables DGI enforcement, tax liens, and seizure of corporate assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) Confirmation Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI - Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUBF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days after the anniversary of incorporation, and within 30 days after any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Imposition of monetary penalties per DGI/RUBF regulations, suspension of the corporation's ability to obtain good-standing and tax certificates; prolonged failure can lead to judicial dissolution and strike-off from the Registro Público.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent certified audit is triggered when a corporation reported total gross revenues exceeding USD 1,000,000 in the preceding fiscal year; mandatory for banks, trust companies, insurance companies, and publicly traded corporations irrespective of revenue
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by Panama for public-interest and large entities; IFRS for SMEs or local Panamanian GAAP (NIF) for smaller private companies; accounting records must be maintained in accordance with the Junta Técnica de Contabilidad

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each Panamanian S.A. must keep a current UBO register at the registered office; regardless of share transfer activity, an annual confirmation is filed through the DGI's RUBF portal within the 30-day anniversary window; every share transfer must be recorded in the Register of Shares and the RUBF record updated within 30 days after transfer
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Officers (Registro de Directores y Oficiales)
Share Transfer Register (Registro de Transferencias de Acciones)
Minute Book of Shareholders' and Directors' Meetings (Libro de Actas)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama applies a territorial income tax system: income derived from Panamanian source is taxed at 25%; income from services rendered and utilized entirely outside Panama may qualify for the 'export of services' exemption under Article 694 of the Código Fiscal, potentially reducing Panamanian CIT to 0% for qualifying data-center colocation services supplied to foreign clients. Additionally, a company licensed under the 'Sede de Empresas Multinacionales' (SEM) regime may obtain CIT exemption for qualifying headquarters services. For entities with no Panamanian-source income, Law 70 of 2019 imposes a fixed annual tax of USD 800 instead of the 25% tax. A minimum tax rule applies: the higher of 25% of net taxable income, 2% of gross taxable income, or the USD 800 fixed tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 20 (Declaración Anual de Renta de Personas Jurídicas) filed through the DGI electronic portal 'e-Tax' (Sistema de Declaración en Línea) at https://etax.mef.gob.pa; each S.A. must have an active RUC. Transfer pricing schedules, when applicable, are attached as Formulario 4126.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be filed within 3 months following the fiscal year-end. A calendar-year taxpayer must file by March 31 of the following year. Advance payments ('pagos a cuenta') computed at 2% of gross revenue are payable in two installments due in June and September of the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RUC number, corporate legal name, fiscal period (Año Fiscal), economic activity code (ISIC 6209), and domicile.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the local resident agent's address and the RUC; the foreign beneficial owner is not separately identified on the return form.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from all sources, including colocation rack-space leasing fees, power metering pass-through charges, cross-connects, remote hands, and monthly recurring hosting fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Panamanian-source revenue is taxable. Revenue from services rendered to foreign clients wholly used abroad should be separately classified as exempt export-of-services revenue and supported by contracts and evidence of foreign receipt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Contra-revenue items including SLA refunds, early-termination discounts, and bad-debt provisions recognized as reductions of gross income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a reconciliation schedule; reductions linked to non-resident customers are acceptable if documented in the colocation contract.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Línea 3 – Ingresos Exentos y No Gravables
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Export-service income eligible for territorial exemption, dividend income from foreign sources, and capital gains from the sale of assets located outside Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Export-service exemption requires that the data-center service be delivered electronically, contracted with a non-resident, and not economically used inside Panama; maintain IP address logs, client domicile certificates, and service-use attestations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs and deductible operating expenses: depreciation of data-center equipment (servers, cooling, UPS, generators), electricity, bandwidth, leased line costs, staff payroll, rent, property insurance, and interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be for the production of Panamanian-source income; cross-border payments to related parties are deductible only if supported by invoices, substantial economic activity, and a transfer-pricing analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sum of deductible items, including the 'Nota Fiscal' provisions, and the capitalized depreciation of qualifying Tier-3/4 infrastructure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident investors are not entitled to personal deductions; all deductions claimed must be evidencable by Panama-based payroll and local vendor documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable net income resulting from gross Panamanian-source revenue minus allowed deductions, before loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 25% rate applies to net taxable income; the 5-year loss carryforward may be applied to offset Panamanian-source profit only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax calculated at 25% of taxable income, subject to the minimum tax rule (2% of gross income or USD 800).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a branch or subsidiary of a non-resident group, the minimum 2% gross-income rule is mitigated if taxable income is fully offset by the loss carryforward; the USD 800 floor always applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Líneas 30–36 – Créditos, Retenciones y Pagos a Cuenta
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits: advanced corporate tax paid (pagos a cuenta), withholding tax certificates (retenciones), tax credits for qualifying reinvestment, and the notional credit for the 5% dividend tax paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders' foreign tax credits are not transferable to the Panamanian entity; the final payment is the difference between the determined tax and the sum of pre-payments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a 10% surcharge on the tax due plus monthly interest of 1% per month (or the fiscal interest rate then in force) on the unpaid balance. Failure to file a zero-income return triggers the mandatory USD 800 annual tax with the same surcharge and interest. Non-filing for three consecutive years can lead the DGI to declare the S.A. 'incumplida', block its operations, and refer the company for cancellation in the Public Registry, in addition to fines of up to USD 5,000 imposed on the resident agent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 4126 – Informe de Precios de Transferencia, filed separately or as an annex to Formulario 20 through the DGI e-Tax portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same statutory deadline as Formulario 20: within 3 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., March 31 for calendar-year taxpayers). Extension of the CIT return does not extend the Form 4126 deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RUC, legal name, fiscal year, aggregate amount of related-party transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transactions with foreign related parties (parent company, sister data-center operators, technology licensors) are reported on an aggregate basis by jurisdiction and type.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Sección B – Operaciones con Partes Relacionadas
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed schedule of intercompany colocation leases, bandwidth purchases, management fees, royalty payments, and interest paid to non-resident affiliates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Each transaction must carry the arm's-length method selected, benchmark comparables, and the internal policy reference; non-resident counterparties do not sign but are identified by TIN and jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Sección C – Método y Conclusión de Rango
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selection of the CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, or Profit Split method, and confirmation that the net margin or price is within the interquartile range.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State that the Panamanian entity derives no unusual loss or low margin relative to independent data-center colocation operators; conclude the taxpayer's position in the arm's-length range.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file Form 4126 when required carries a fine of up to 1% of the related-party transaction value, not less than USD 5,000; understatement of income or inflating deductions due to non-arm's-length pricing can generate a tax assessment of 25% plus the 10% surcharge, monthly interest, and possible criminal referral for fraudulent returns.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% withholding at the shareholder level on dividend distributions to residents and non-residents. Instead, the distributing Panamanian S.A. bears a 5% 'Impuesto sobre Dividendos' on dividends paid out of profits derived from Panamanian-source income. If the S.A. has fully paid the 25% corporate income tax on the distributed profits, the dividend tax is effectively creditable/eliminated. Dividends paid from foreign-source (territorial exempt) profits are entirely excluded from the dividend tax. Thus, a non-resident data-center investor can repatriate net profits at a maximum effective burden of 25% CIT plus, where relevant, a minor dividend tax on the residual; no additional dividend WHT is levied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama's DTA network (in force with Barbados, France, Italy, Luxembourg, Mexico, Netherlands, Portugal, Qatar, Singapore, South Korea, Spain, UAE, and the UK) does not apply to reduce the dividend WHT because no shareholder-level withholding exists. To invoke any treaty reduction on royalties, interest, or technical-service payments, the non-resident recipient must: (i) be the beneficial owner and a tax resident of the treaty state; (ii) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the foreign tax authority; (iii) submit the TRC plus a Form 50/Solicitud de Trato Convencional to the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) before or at the time of filing Formulario 20; and (iv) maintain a sworn statement and supporting contracts demonstrating no conduit arrangement. Without a valid TRC, the statutory 12.5% withholding on Panamanian-source royalties/technical fees applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding: royalties and technical-service payments made by a Panamanian payer to a non-resident for rights/services used in Panama are subject to 12.5% withholding (Código Fiscal Art. 261). Cross-border debt interest paid to non-resident lenders is not subject to Panamanian withholding. Treaty rates typically cap royalties at 5%-10% (e.g., UK, Netherlands, France, Luxembourg) and interest at 0%-10%, provided the beneficial ownership and TRC tests are met. For data-center colocation, software licensing embedded in rack-lease fees is characterized as business profit and may be exempt unless a separate royalty component is expressly contracted.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD (Balboa) 250,000: Formulario 4126 and a formal Local File study are mandatory when the aggregate annual value of transactions with related parties equals or exceeds USD 250,000. A Master File is required for multinational groups with consolidated group revenue equal to or above USD 5,000,000, and the Panamanian entity must also file Form 4126 if it engages in related-party transactions above the USD 250,000 threshold. A contemporaneous transfer-pricing study must be prepared by the filing date; penalties apply for absence or late preparation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama has not enacted a standalone Economic Substance Regulations statute equivalent to the BVI/Cayman model. However, Law 70 of 2019 and DGI administrative criteria require an S.A. invoking the territorial 'export of services' exemption or an offshore income exclusion to evidence genuine economic activity: a physical data-center facility in Panama, local contracted employees or responsible officers, operational decision-making in Panama, and the actual generation of revenue through servers physically located in Panamanian territory. Non-resident-owned S.A.s that hold colocation contracts and bank accounts but lack any local operational presence, employees, or power/network utilities are treated as shell entities; the DGI may disregard the corporate form, reclassify all global income as Panamanian-source, assess 25% plus penalties, and impose interest. Since 2015, Law 23 of 2015 also requires all legal entities to maintain minimal accounting records; failure to present these records to the DGI triggers administrative fines and supports the presumption that the entity is a facade.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately classifying Panamanian-source colocation income as 'offshore export services' and failing to file Formulario 20, understating gross revenue, or destroying records that demonstrate revenue earned from domestic clients.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Surcharge of 10% of the tax due plus monthly interest of 1%; under Law 23 of 2015 and Article 279 of the Código Penal, tax evasion is a criminal offense punishable by imprisonment of 2 to 5 years and a fine of 2 to 5 times the evaded tax; the DGI may redetermine taxable income by factoring external indicators and apply the 2% gross-income minimum.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers, and the resident agent who knowingly sign false returns are criminally liable; civil restitution of the evaded tax plus interest is imposed personally, and the DGI can obtain an 'Aviso de Salida' (departure prohibition) against them to prevent flight, alongside asset seizures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a nominee-owned S.A. that invoices data-center colocation fees but has no physical Tier-3/4 facility, no staff, no electricity contracts in Panama, and no local books; claiming the USD 800 fixed-tax regime while operating servers abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI will apply the 'levantamiento del velo corporativo' (piercing the corporate veil), reclassify all income as Panamanian-source, assess 25% tax, add the 10% surcharge and monthly interest, and impose fines under Law 70/2019; the S.A. may be administratively dissolved and struck from the Public Registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shareholders who use the shell to evade tax are personally liable for the full assessed tax; courts may order travel bans, freeze Panamanian bank accounts, and impose sentences of 2 to 5 years under the tax-evasion statute, with a further penalty for violation of the beneficial-ownership registry rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Failure to Maintain Minimal Accounting Records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to keep books and records, client KYC files, or transaction documentation as required by Law 23 of 2015 and Law 129 of 2013; accepting undisclosed wire transfers without verifying the source of funds for the data-center payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines of up to USD 1,000,000 per violation under Law 23/2015 for legal entities; the S.A. can be barred from banking activity; money laundering charges under Article 254 of the Código Penal carry imprisonment of 5 to 10 years, extended to 12 years for aggravated amounts or criminal-organization involvement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Compliance officers, directors, and the beneficial owner are subject to personal criminal prosecution; the court can issue travel bans, freezing orders, and forfeiture of corporate assets; civil liability extends to restitution of laundered funds, and directors found to have knowingly ignored AML controls can be incarcerated for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring intercompany colocation lease payments, bandwidth fees, or management charges with a non-resident affiliate at non-arm's-length rates to shift profit out of Panama; failing to file Formulario 4126 when related-party transactions exceed USD 250,000; claiming the 12.5% foreign technical fee deduction without a transfer-pricing study.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI may reprice each transaction using the most appropriate OECD method, disallow deductions for the excessive portion, assess 25% tax on the upward adjustment, apply the 10% surcharge and monthly interest, and levy a fine of up to 1% of the transaction value (minimum USD 5,000) for the missing Form 4126.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or approve the non-arm's-length intercompany contracts are jointly and severally liable for the additional tax, interest, and penalties; in cases of documentation fraud or false certification, directors face criminal tax-evasion charges with imprisonment of 2 to 5 years and a departure ban pending resolution.
